issues.description: The generated flags field redundantly combines a `ghost` field marker with the `Ghost<T>` wrapper type.
issues.rationale: The field is declared as `ghost flags: Ghost<Set<...>>`, expressing the same proof-only mode twice. The human reviewer explicitly required choosing either the `ghost` marker or the `Ghost` wrapper, and the author agreed. The human-approved follow-up commit removes the field marker and retains the wrapper. The repository later codified this convention as `avoid-redundant-mode-markers`; that later fixed guideline is used for present adjudication and is not claimed to have existed at the historical review commit.

issues.description: The exported macro's Clone implementation uses an unqualified `Ghost` constructor and unconditionally evaluates a ghost-only specification, breaking downstream or documentation builds where that name or ghost code is unavailable.
issues.rationale: `bitflags!` is exported and expands in downstream crates, but `clone` constructs `flags` with the bare identifier `Ghost` without importing or fully qualifying it in that scope. It also calls `Self::flags_from_bits` unconditionally even though the same revision explicitly gates the analogous initialization in `from_bits_unchecked` for doc/non-`verus_keep_ghost` builds. Thus expansion can fail name resolution at a call site, or reintroduce the documentation-build failure the patch is intended to avoid. The initial report was automated, so it is not accepted on that basis alone: the exact follow-up commit `0a22c7f44e967b51d14cfbfbd8fc996570939722` replaces this expression with `flags: self.flags`, and a human reviewer approved that commit.
